title: Interactive Stamp System and Responsive Token Fallbacks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Dashboard panels and rollout rails currently depend on multiple one-off badge components for status, capacity, and cost flags. These badges (chips/pills/stamps) behave inconsistently across density modes and break visual hierarchy at small widths or when the customer enables compact density.

Goal: Define a compact, flexible "stamp" component family with a prescriptive responsive token fallback strategy so stamps remain legible and semantically consistent across console views (metrics cards, rollout rails, allocation lists). Deliver a Figma library of variants, a token map (color/typography/spacing/contrast fallbacks), accessibility guidance, and a short dev spec for implementation in the component library.

Scope: Visual system for stamps (status, warning, info, trial, committed), sizing rules for three density breakpoints, interaction states (hover/focus/pressed), icon + text combinations, and a token fallback matrix to drive automatic substitution when typography or palette tokens change. Also includes QA checklist and retrofittable migration notes for existing stamp usages in dashboards and rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library with stamp component variants (default/compact/condensed) published to Console Kit and linked in this ticket
Token fallback matrix documented (primary token -> medium contrast fallback -> high contrast fallback) for color and typography
Accessibility: each variant meets 4.5:1 contrast for text or provides an accessible alternative (icon-only + aria-label) where text is removed in compact mode
Design handoff note with CSS/SCSS token names and a minimal JS behavior outline for truncation and aria attributes
Prototype demonstrating stamp resizing across three density states and a sample dashboard with mixed stamps
comments: 2025-02-18 | Ava Chen: Initial discovery — audit of 42 stamp usages across console completed. Found 3 distinct visual styles in the wild and 2 code components (BadgeV1, FlagV2). Logged instances and exported screenshots to the spec page.

2025-02-21 | Priya Singh: Sketched responsive variants in Figma. Proposed three density breakpoints: roomy, default, compact. Compact removes text for low-importance stamps and switches to icon with tooltip/aria-label. Posting sketches in Figma.

2025-02-24 | Diego Morales (Frontend): Noted runtime constraints: some list renderers strip embedded tooltips for perf. We should include a programmatic fallback to expose aria-labels where tooltips are unavailable.

2025-02-26 | Accessibility review (Marisol Torres): Recommended contrast fallbacks and suggested that icon-only compact stamps must maintain 3:1 contrast with the background and provide visible focus ring at 2px.

2025-03-01 | Priya Singh: Updated token fallback table after contrast tests. Consolidated color tokens from 6 to 4 canonical semantic tokens for stamps: stamp-success, stamp-warning, stamp-info, stamp-neutral.

2025-03-03 | PM feedback (Liam O'Connor): Prioritize rollouts and allocation lists for migration (high customer visibility). Suggested a canary rollout on dedicated accounts followed by a gradual migration plan. Adding release notes to console-2025.04
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Opted to remove text on the smallest density to preserve layout — tradeoff is discoverability mitigated by consistent iconography and tooltips/aria-labels
Chose semantic token names (stamp-success etc.) rather than contextual color tokens to simplify developer selection and future theme mapping
Deferred animated micro-interactions (pulse on new stamp) to a follow-up ticket to avoid scope creep for the initial release
next_steps: Finalize Figma library and export tokens to design tokens registry
Align with frontend on token names and small CSS spec (padding, min-width, border-radius) — schedule a pairing session
Create migration PR checklist and a canary rollout plan with telemetry hooks (stamp-render-count, truncation-events)
QA pass across compact/default/roomy density on Chrome/Safari/Firefox and mobile viewports
